why: The student says the file can be renamed to Greeting.java while it still holds public class hello, but Java requires a public class to be in a file with the same name, so this is the 'class name and file name are independent' misconception.

concepts.quote: I can rename the file to Greeting.java and keep public class hello.
concepts.why: This treats the public class name as separate from the file name, but public class hello must be in hello.java.

concepts.quote: rename the file to Greeting.java and keep public class hello
concepts.why: This uses the wrong rule that the source file can have any name, but javac rejects a public class hello saved in Greeting.java.
